messages.content: All 16 share one fingerprint. Let me read one report and the code.

The panic is in `parseBearer`: a header of exactly `Bearer` (no trailing space) makes `SplitN` return one element, and `[1]` panics. Issue #103 already describes this. I'll check the history, confirm the other reports share the same header shape, and read the issue's comments.
Issue #103 is open and describes this exact crash, so this group is a duplicate. The current code still has the bug, so I'll add the root-cause analysis to #103 rather than filing a new issue.

function.name: notes_write
function.arguments: {"group": "fp_6b14b3", "note": "16 reports (cr_3586c4 and 15 others), all v1.4.0 (commit 9c41e7a), all POST /v1/reminders with \"Authorization: Bearer\" (no token). Root cause: auth/auth.go:66 parseBearer does strings.SplitN(h, \" \", 2)[1]; a header of exactly \"Bearer\" has no space, so the slice has length 1. Introduced in d093827 (baseline). Matches open issue #103, filed without investigation. Status: duplicate of #103. Not fixed here per the duplicate rule. Unrelated #101 (schedule.parseClock, fp_6a907a) shares only the panic text."}

function.name: issue_comment
function.arguments: {"id": 103, "body": "Root cause found (fp_6b14b3, 16 reports, all v1.4.0, all POST /v1/reminders with the header exactly \"Authorization: Bearer\"). auth/auth.go:66 in parseBearer does strings.SplitN(h, \" \", 2)[1]. The prefix check only tests HasPrefix(h, \"Bearer\"), so \"Bearer\" with no trailing space and no token passes it, and SplitN returns one element. Fix: require the form \"Bearer <token>\" with a non-empty token, and return false otherwise, so the API answers 401 instead of panicking. Introduced in d093827 (v1.4.0 baseline)."}
